PLAINTIFF’S MOTION FOR LEAVE TO FILE NOTICE OF
SUBSEQUENT RECORD DEVELOPMENT RELEVANT TO
PENDING RULE 72(a) OBJECTIONS

Plaintiff Marvelle J. Ballentine moves under Local Civil Rule 7(F)(1) for leave to file the
Notice of Subsequent Record Development attached as Exhibit A. In support, Plaintiff states as
follows.

1. Plaintiff’s Rule 72(a) Objections are pending. ECF No. 66. The objections
challenge, among other matters, the requirement in ECF No. 64 that Plaintiff provide a redlined
comparison of the proposed Second Amended and Supplemental Complaint.

2. On September 18, 2026, after the objections were filed, Defendants Katie Hall and
the National Center for Missing & Exploited Children (“NCMEC”) filed their opposition to

Plaintiff’s motion for leave to amend. ECF No. 74. ECF No. 74 states that, “despite numerous

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-IDD Document 76 Filed 09/18/26 Page 2 of 6 PagelD# 765

efforts, undersigned counsel has been unable to ‘reverse-engineer’ a redline comparison of the two
documents via either Adobe or Word.” ECF No. 74 at 4.

3. Local Civil Rule 7(F)(1) provides that no further briefs or written communications
may be filed without leave of Court. Plaintiff seeks that leave. A Memorandum in Support
accompanies this motion.

Plaintiff submits this motion on the papers and waives oral argument on this motion only.
The waiver does not alter any request for oral argument made in ECF No. 66.

WHEREFORE, Plaintiff requests an order granting leave, deeming the attached Notice
filed, and providing for its consideration with ECF No. 66. A proposed order accompanies this

motion.

Date: September 18, 2026 Respectfully submitted,

rp

Marvelle J. Ballentine

Plaintiff, pro se

GENERATIVE-ARTIFICIAL-INTELLIGENCE DISCLOSURE AND

CITATION CERTIFICATION PURSUANT TO ECF NOS. 63 AND 65

Pursuant to the Orders entered September 9, 2026 (ECF No. 63) and September 10, 2026
(ECF No. 65), Plaintiff states as follows.

1. Identification of use. Plaintiff used generative artificial intelligence in the
preparation of the Motion, Exhibit A (the Notice of Subsequent Record Development), and the
Proposed Order submitted with this filing. The assistance consisted of research, drafting, and
revision of text; retrieval of docket entries and filed documents from the public RECAP archive;
and verification of record citations against the docket. Plaintiff reviewed, edited, and adopted each
document as his own submission. The Proposed Order is covered by this certification and carries
no separate certification on its face. The Memorandum in Support is separately filed and carries its
own disclosure and certification.

2. Citation review. Plaintiff certifies that he has reviewed each citation to legal
authority and each citation to the record in the documents identified in paragraph 1 for accuracy.
Plaintiff performed that review using automated citation-verification tools to verify cited
authorities against published sources and by comparing each record citation to the document as
docketed.

3. Method. ECF Nos. 63 and 65 do not specify the form or placement of this
disclosure. Plaintiff places the disclosure and certification in each motion filing and separately
docketed memorandum, with the motion’s certification expressly covering the AlI-assisted
attachments identified in paragraph 1. Plaintiff supplies this disclosure and certification while

maintaining the authority-and-scope objection stated in Part IX of the Memorandum in Support of

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-IDD Document 76 Filed 09/18/26 Page 6 of 6 PagelD# 769

his Rule 72(a) Objections. ECF No. 68. Plaintiff requests approval of this method, or specification
of a different method, for any requirement that remains in effect.
